steps.stem: Adi, who owns a bookshop, had its lighting replaced with bright white lamps in the hope of attracting more customers. Three weeks later she was disappointed to find that sales had declined, and she attributed the decline to the new lighting. Which of the following facts would support Adi's explanation?
choices: Adi's bookshop specializes in rare books that are hard to find anywhere else in the city
The pharmacy across the street from Adi's shop is lit by bright white lamps and is always crowded
Ten days before Adi had the lamps replaced, a large bookstore offering steep discounts opened on the same street
In Adi's two other bookshops, where the lighting was not replaced, sales did not change during the same period
explanation: Shops without the new lighting saw no change, so the lighting is what set the declining shop apart. (1) is irrelevant, (2) is a counterexample, and (3) offers another cause of the decline.

steps.stem: Ruth saw her neighbor, Mr. Adler, leave several wooden chairs painted bright yellow on the sidewalk for the garbage collectors. She concluded that Mr. Adler does not like yellow furniture. Which of the following statements does not weaken Ruth's conclusion?
choices: Every piece of furniture in Mr. Adler's apartment is painted yellow
The chairs Mr. Adler put out had cracked or wobbly legs
Mr. Adler received the yellow chairs as a gift a month before his wedding
Mr. Adler's daughter had recently bought him a new dining set
explanation: When and how he got the chairs says nothing about why he threw them out. (1), (2) and (4) each give a reason other than dislike of yellow.

steps.stem: In an experiment, Dr. Elkin formed two teams of volunteers – a team of three and a team of nine – and gave each team one hour to find, working together, as many as possible of the small objects hidden in a garden; each team searched a different garden of the same size. The team of nine found far more objects than the team of three, and Dr. Elkin hypothesized that the number of members in a team affects its success at this type of task. Which of the following statements strengthens Dr. Elkin's hypothesis?
choices: One of the members of the team of nine had helped hide the objects before the experiment and remembered where several of them were
The members of the team of three had often taken part in such searches, whereas the members of the team of nine had never done so
Six of the members of the team of nine were called away before their team had begun searching the garden
The garden searched by the team of three was far more densely overgrown than the garden searched by the team of nine
explanation: The larger team won even though experience was on the smaller team's side, which rules out experience as the explanation. (1) and (4) give rival explanations, and (3) means the teams were really the same size.

steps.stem: Given: The proportion of people with dry skin among those who use the cream Dermalin is higher than the proportion among the general population. Hypothesis: Dry skin is a side effect of using Dermalin. Which of the following findings weakens the hypothesis?
choices: People who use an alternative cream to Dermalin do not suffer from dry skin
Dermatologists may recommend Dermalin only to people who do not have dry skin
Dermalin is a cream for relieving the itching caused by dry skin
One of the common side effects of Dermalin is a mild rash
explanation: If Dermalin is used because of dry skin, the dry skin comes first and the cream follows: cause and effect are reversed. (2) supports the hypothesis, and (1) and (4) do not bear on it.

steps.stem: At dinner Noam ate a very spicy curry, and soon afterwards his mouth began to burn. Twenty minutes later he ate a portion of the dessert "Kolara," and the burning stopped. Noam concluded from this that vanilla, one of the ingredients of "Kolara," neutralizes the effect of hot spices. Which of the following does not weaken Noam's conclusion?
choices: Noam drinks vanilla-flavored coffee almost every day, and it has never caused a burning sensation in his mouth
"Kolara" is made with a large amount of cream, and dairy products are known to ease the burning caused by hot spices
According to the chef, the burning caused by the spices in the curry Noam ate usually fades by itself within about ten minutes
The curry Noam ate contained hardly any hot spices, but it was seasoned with an herb to which Noam is sensitive, and his sensitivity shows itself as a burning sensation in the mouth
explanation: That vanilla does not cause burning says nothing about whether it relieves burning caused by spices. (2) offers another active ingredient, (3) the passage of time, and (4) another cause of the burning.

steps.stem: At a certain youth soccer club, players who miss a practice without notice are recorded by the club secretary and are also given a penalty: at the next practice they must help the equipment manager collect and wash the balls. Last month the equipment manager was on leave, and the number of unexcused absences recorded was much lower than usual. The club director concluded that helping the equipment manager does not deter players from missing practice, since they enjoy his company. Which of the following facts may weaken the director's conclusion?
choices: Two months ago a record was set both in the number of unexcused absences and in the number of players sent to help the equipment manager
At the start of last month the club announced that the team with the fewest unexcused absences this season would travel to a tournament abroad
When the equipment manager returned from leave, the number of unexcused absences went up again
Last month the players' school exam period began, which makes it harder for them to find time for practice
explanation: A prize announced at the same time offers another reason for the drop in absences. (3) supports the director, (4) should have raised absences, so the drop despite it also supports the conclusion, and (1) says nothing about last month.

steps.title: Strengthen and weaken: the toolkit
steps.intro: Every choice adds data. Ask which way it pushes the conclusion.

head: Weakens
Strengthens
rows: !Alternative explanation – another reason for the same data
!Negating an alternative explanation – the other reason is ruled out (or works against the result)
Counterexample – the cause without the effect
Supporting example – no cause, no effect
Chicken and egg – cause and effect swapped
Undermining the basis – the data behind the conclusion is shaky
Strengthening the basis – the data becomes even stronger

tips: Gambler test: bet on the conclusion. Does the new fact shake your bet?
'Does not weaken': cross out the 3 that weaken. The answer may be irrelevant, not only strengthening.
Flip test: if the flipped fact weakens, the original strengthens.
Watch whether the data is a number or a percentage.
A clear-cut alternative explanation: mark it and move on.

steps.stem: In city A, researchers tested whether four-year-olds understand that another person may hold a false belief. Each child watched a puppet put a ball into a box and leave the room; the ball was then moved to a basket, and the child was asked where the puppet would look for the ball when it returned. Most of the children answered "in the box." When the experiment was repeated in city B, most of the children answered "in the basket." The researchers concluded that in city B the understanding that others may hold false beliefs develops later than in city A. Which of the following findings does not weaken the researchers' conclusion?
choices: In city B, children tend to take a question about where someone will look for an object as asking where the object is
Puppets are rare in city B, and children there do not see them as characters with thoughts
In city A many more children than in city B have hearing difficulties that make spoken stories hard to follow
In another test, children from city B, unlike those from city A, correctly predicted where a friend who had not seen a toy moved would look for it
explanation: Hearing difficulties would make the task harder in city A, so A's success despite them leaves the conclusion intact. (4) shows the understanding present in city B, and (1) and (2) explain the children's answers in city B without any difference in understanding.

steps.stem: The director of a botanical garden brought a rare orchid from another garden, hoping that it would flower. For four months the plant produced no flowers, and the director moved it to a greenhouse with much higher humidity; shortly afterwards it flowered. The director concluded that the plants in the garden need high humidity in order to flower. Which of the following facts would weaken the director's conclusion?
choices: The previous orchid brought to the garden had not been moved to a greenhouse
Orchids of this kind are rarely found growing in dense clusters in the wild
Before coming to the garden, the orchid had grown for years in a climate like the garden's
Orchids of this kind flower only after a long period of adjusting to a new place
explanation: If the orchid needed time rather than humidity, the flowering after four months and a move is explained by the time alone. (3) removes the need for adjustment and so supports the director, and (1) and (2) do not bear on the cause.

steps.stem: Ofir read in a local newspaper that in 2019 attendance at the Marom Jazz Festival did not rise compared with the previous year, although early that year the festival's organizers had launched a wide advertising campaign on radio and online. He judged that the reason is that the festival grounds are too small to hold more visitors. Which of the following facts would weaken Ofir's judgment?
choices: In 2018 the festival grounds were never filled to capacity, not even on the busiest evening of the festival
At the end of 2019 the organizers decided to move the festival to larger grounds
In 2019 tickets to the festival were cheaper than they had been in 2018
Listeners' reactions to the organizers' advertising campaign were very favorable
explanation: If there was spare room the year before, lack of space is not what kept attendance flat. (2) concerns a later change, and (3) and (4) make the flat figure more puzzling without bearing on the space.

steps.stem: Researchers compared two kinds of restaurant reviews to find out which influences diners more: reviews written by well-known food critics and reviews written by anonymous diners. They found that a restaurant praised by a well-known critic received more reservations in the following month than a restaurant praised by anonymous diners, and they summed up their conclusion in the title of their article: "A Famous Name Fills the Tables." Which of the following statements could weaken the researchers' conclusion?
choices: A review by a well-known local critic is no less influential than a review by a well-known foreign critic
Well-known critics generally review only restaurants that are already among the most popular in their city
In printed magazines, unlike on websites, most restaurant reviews are written by well-known critics
Readers suspect that anonymous reviews are written by the restaurants' owners, and this makes them distrust such reviews
explanation: If the critics choose restaurants that are already popular, the gap in reservations has another cause. (4) offers a mechanism that supports the conclusion, and (1) and (3) do not bear on the comparison.

steps.stem: About eight years ago, several car insurance companies in the country of Nordavia began to require drivers under the age of twenty-five to install in their cars a device that beeps whenever the car exceeds the speed limit. Recently the traffic authority reported that over the past eight years the number of accidents involving drivers under twenty-five fell by fifteen percent, and officials proposed a law requiring every driver to install the device, arguing that this would reduce accidents among all drivers. Critics of the argument suggested that several questions be investigated first. Which of the following investigations is not relevant to testing the officials' argument?
choices: Over the past eight years, did the number of drivers over twenty-five whose cars are fitted with the device increase?
Over the past eight years, did the proportion of drivers under twenty-five who took an advanced driving course increase?
Did the fall in accidents apply only to young drivers whose cars were fitted with the device?
Over the past eight years, did the number of accidents fall among all drivers, or only among drivers under twenty-five?
explanation: How many older drivers installed the device has no bearing on why accidents among young drivers fell. (2) tests a rival cause, (3) tests whether the device is the cause, and (4) tests whether the fall is general.

steps.stem: A study found that children who ate breakfast at the same hour every morning had higher grades than children who did not eat breakfast at a fixed hour. Following the study, a school principal sent the parents a letter recommending that their children eat breakfast at a fixed hour. A child psychologist argued that the recommendation was unjustified, basing her argument on a certain piece of information. Which of the following is most likely to be the information on which the psychologist relied?
choices: Eating breakfast at one particular hour is not necessarily more beneficial than eating it at another
The grades of the children in the study were, on the whole, lower than the national average
Children whose home life is orderly, and whose parents follow their studies closely, tend to eat breakfast at a fixed hour
Most parents do not follow the recommendations that schools send home
explanation: The children who keep a fixed hour come from homes that also support their studies, so the higher grades may be due to the home rather than the hour. (1) repeats the doubt without grounding it, and (2) and (4) do not bear on the comparison.

steps.stem: The mayor of a city claims that vandalism in the city's parks increased this year compared with last year. As evidence he points out that park wardens filed significantly more reports of vandalism this year than they did last year. Which of the following pieces of information shows that the evidence the mayor cites cannot, on its own, establish his claim?
choices: Last year the city carried out a surprise inspection of all its parks to locate damaged equipment
Many of the wardens who filed reports this year had themselves been assigned to repair the damage
Last year the city invested heavily in fences and lighting to prevent vandalism in its parks
Early this year the city gave the wardens an app that lets them file a report in seconds instead of filling out a paper form
explanation: More reports may reflect easier reporting rather than more vandalism. (3) supports the mayor, and (1) and (2) do not bear on the number of reports.

steps.stem: Dr. Stern: "Hikers estimate how long they have been walking by how tired they feel." Dr. Eilon: "Hikers estimate how long they have been walking by the number of landmarks they have passed." Which of the following findings weakens Dr. Stern's claim without strengthening Dr. Eilon's?
choices: Hikers with heavy packs and hikers with no packs estimate their walking time equally accurately
Hikers on featureless trails estimate their walking time less accurately than others
Hikers find it hard to estimate walking times longer than five hours
Hikers estimate their walking time less accurately at night than by day
explanation: Equal accuracy despite very different levels of effort tells against tiredness and says nothing about landmarks. (2) and (4) strengthen Dr. Eilon, and (3) bears on neither claim.

steps.stem: Dr. Navon noticed that a large share of the patients who come to his clinic with the eye disease "tzarevet" are long-distance truck drivers. He concluded that driving for many hours encourages the outbreak of the disease. Which of the following would strengthen Dr. Navon's conclusion?
choices: Dr. Navon's clinic is located next to the country's largest truck depot
Staring at the road for hours reduces blinking, and reduced blinking is suspected of causing the disease
A study found that the disease tends to run in families
Driving for many hours causes eye strain, and the disease also causes eye strain
explanation: A mechanism links long driving to the disease. (1) explains the observation without the cause, (3) offers a different cause, and (4) mistakes a shared symptom for a link.

steps.stem: The pupils of Ms. Kedar's piano class and the pupils of Mr. Zohar's piano class took part in the same regional competition, and the average score of Ms. Kedar's pupils was higher. The director of the music school supposed that Ms. Kedar's teaching methods are better than Mr. Zohar's; the deputy director supposed instead that Ms. Kedar's pupils practice at home more than Mr. Zohar's do. Which of the following data would weaken both suppositions?
choices: A third class, also taught by Mr. Zohar, scored lower on average than Ms. Kedar's class and higher than Mr. Zohar's first class
In a theory examination, for which both classes had the same teacher, Mr. Zohar's pupils scored higher than Ms. Kedar's
Two months before the competition Ms. Kedar went on leave, and Mr. Zohar taught both classes
Most of Ms. Kedar's pupils had played the piano for years before joining her class, whereas Mr. Zohar's pupils were all beginners
explanation: Prior experience is a third cause of the gap, neither the teacher's methods nor the pupils' practice. (2) tells against the practice explanation only, and (1) and (3) bear on the teacher only.

steps.stem: "Midnight Harbor," the second album of the band Kestrel, sold far fewer copies than the band's first album, "Salt Roads." The record company judged that the second album sold less because it was priced higher than the first. Which of the following facts does not weaken the record company's judgment?
choices: "Salt Roads" was released with a music video that was widely broadcast on television, whereas "Midnight Harbor" had no video
The songs on "Midnight Harbor" are long and slow, whereas those on "Salt Roads" are short, lively songs well suited to radio
The band's third album, "Glass Tide," was priced lower than both earlier albums and sold more copies than either
Unlike "Midnight Harbor," "Salt Roads" came out just before the holiday season, when many people buy albums as gifts
explanation: A cheaper album that sold more is just what the price explanation predicts. (1), (2) and (4) each supply a different cause of the difference in sales.

steps.stem: A study conducted in the country of Norland found that over the past fifteen years the rate of "nishtefet," a skin disease that causes a temporary rash, has been higher in the port city of Veltra than in the country's other cities. The researchers supposed that the reason is the high humidity in Veltra. Which of the following facts does not weaken the researchers' supposition?
choices: Veltra's drinking water contains a high level of chlorine, and chlorine raises the risk of contracting the disease
The disease mainly affects young children, and the proportion of young children in Veltra's population is lower than the national average
Until a dam was built near Veltra three years ago, the humidity in the city was low
The humidity in the city of Arnes is higher than in Veltra, but the rate of the disease there is very low
explanation: Fewer young children makes Veltra's high rate harder to explain but offers no rival cause. (1) offers one, (3) breaks the timing, and (4) breaks the link between humidity and the disease.

steps.stem: A plan has been proposed to build a large parking garage in the center of a city, which will make it easier for drivers to find parking there and so shorten the time they spend circling in search of a space. Opponents of the plan argue that the garage, if built, will increase traffic congestion in the city center. Which of the following facts does not support the opponents' claim?
choices: The easier it is to park somewhere, the more people drive there instead of using public transportation
The more parking a city center offers, the more cars enter it
Cars entering and leaving a large garage cause lines on nearby streets
The longer drivers search for parking, the heavier the congestion in the streets
explanation: A garage that shortens the search would, by (4), reduce congestion, the opposite of the opponents' claim. (1), (2) and (3) each supply a route from the garage to more congestion.

steps.stem: In an international survey, workers in different countries were asked to rate their satisfaction with their jobs on a scale from one to ten, and the average satisfaction of the workers in Lundia was higher than that of the workers in Sarvia. Professor Weiss argues that one cannot conclude from the survey that there is a gap in job satisfaction between the workers of the two countries. Which of the following is best suited to be the basis of her argument?
choices: In Sarvian culture it is considered immodest to express great satisfaction, and people who are very pleased with something tend to call it merely "acceptable"
Wages in Lundia are higher than in Sarvia, and the higher a person's wage, the more satisfied they are with their job
The share of respondents who chose "6" among the Lundian respondents was equal to the share among the Sarvian respondents
Because of an error, several hundred Lundian questionnaires were not counted, and the average satisfaction among those respondents was higher than among the other Lundians
explanation: If the two cultures use the scale differently, the numbers do not measure the same thing. (2) supports the gap, (4) would widen it, and (3) is beside the point.

steps.stem: Irit, who runs the "Tempo" dance studio, noticed that only a few of the studio's students are over fifty. She assumed that the reason is that people over fifty are less interested in dancing than younger people. Her assistant, Moshe, pointed out a fact that led Irit to change her mind. Which of the following is most likely to be the fact Moshe pointed out?
choices: The "Tempo" studio is small and poorly ventilated, and it offers only a few styles of dance
Across the street from "Tempo" is the busy "Rhythm" studio, the only studio in the city that offers classes designed especially for people over fifty
The rival studio "Salsa Club" began to offer a reduced price to people over fifty, but this did not increase their number among its students
Among the students at "Tempo," the share of those in their twenties is higher than the share of those in their thirties
explanation: People over fifty are dancing, but elsewhere. (3) supports Irit's assumption, and (1) and (4) do not bear on that age group's interest in dancing.

steps.stem: A study of the leaves of the karva shrub found that a tea made from them improves concentration. The researchers supposed that delta, one of the substances in the leaves, is responsible for the effect. However, participants who swallowed capsules containing delta showed no similar improvement, and the researchers therefore concluded that their supposition had been mistaken. Which of the following findings would strengthen the researchers' conclusion?
choices: Participants who drank tea made from karva leaves from which the delta had been removed improved their concentration as much as participants who drank ordinary karva tea
The concentration of participants who drank tea made from karva leaves that contain no delta did not improve
Participants who drank karva tea were, on average, more tired than participants who did not
The capsules also contained another substance, epsilon, which blocks the action of delta
explanation: If the tea works just as well without delta, delta is not the cause. (2) supports the original supposition, (4) rescues it by explaining the capsules' failure, and (3) is beside the point.

steps.stem: For two weeks Eyal read the local newspaper every day and noticed that it did not report a single traffic accident in the town. He concluded that no traffic accidents had occurred there during those two weeks. Which of the following facts would weaken Eyal's conclusion?
choices: The local newspaper makes a point of covering every event in the town
In those two weeks nothing happened that could have pushed accident reports out of the paper
The town's roads were crowded during those weeks, and accidents could have occurred
The local newspaper reports traffic accidents only in a monthly supplement
explanation: If the daily paper never carries accident reports, its silence proves nothing. (1) and (2) strengthen Eyal's inference, and (3) shows only that accidents were possible, not that they happened.

steps.stem: Until the middle of the twentieth century the inhabitants of the island of Tarvo drank almost no coffee, and few cases of the heart condition "palpeset" were recorded among them. Today, now that coffee has become the island's most popular drink, the island's clinics record a marked rise in the number of cases of the condition. From this, researchers concluded that drinking coffee raises the risk of palpeset. Which of the following facts would weaken the researchers' conclusion?
choices: Life expectancy on Tarvo is still among the highest in the region
The instruments that the island's clinics use to detect heart conditions have improved greatly over the past seventy years
Among islanders who moved to the mainland, where coffee is widely drunk, the rate of palpeset is similar to that of the mainland population
Compared with the middle of the twentieth century, far fewer islanders suffer from headaches today, and coffee is known to relieve headaches
explanation: More recorded cases may mean better detection rather than more disease. (3) supports the conclusion, and (1) and (4) do not bear on it.

steps.stem: Ofra wanted to find out which of eight sample paint colors her grandparents would like best for their living room. She showed them the eight samples one after another and asked them to give each one a score, the highest score going to the color they found most pleasing. When she added up the results, Ofra found that the color with the highest score was the lightest one. Which of the following facts casts doubt on the reliability of Ofra's test?
choices: Ofra's grandmother said the room grew dark while they were scoring, and she could hardly tell the last samples apart
Ofra's grandfather paints landscapes as a hobby
Ofra's grandmother says that her favorite color is sky blue, which was not among the eight samples
Ofra's grandparents seldom sit in their living room
explanation: If the last samples could not be seen properly, the scores do not compare like with like. (2), (3) and (4) do not affect how the samples were scored.

steps.stem: A company offered its sales staff an optional negotiation workshop. At the end of the quarter the sales manager found that those who had attended did not close more deals than those who had not, and concluded that the workshop was useless. Which of the following data could cause the manager to retract his conclusion?
choices: The only employees who did not attend the workshop were those who were away on business trips at the time
The employees who attended the workshop are the company's most experienced and ambitious salespeople
Employees of another company who attended a similar workshop closed fewer deals, on average, than those who did not
The employees with the strongest sales records chose not to attend the workshop, preferring to spend the time with clients
explanation: If the strongest salespeople stayed away, equal results mean the workshop lifted the weaker ones. (2) makes the equal results even worse for the workshop, and (1) and (3) do not bear on it.

steps.stem: An agricultural company wished to test a new fertilizer for tomatoes. It compared two plots: both received the same irrigation and care, but one was also treated with the fertilizer. At harvest the plants in the treated plot yielded more tomatoes, on average, than the plants in the other plot, and the company concluded that the fertilizer increases the yield. Which of the following data does not weaken the company's conclusion?
choices: Besides the fertilizer, the treated plot received more hours of direct sunlight than the other plot
Before the trial the soil in the treated plot was richer than the soil in the other plot
The company's researchers do not yet know which of the fertilizer's ingredients is responsible for its effect
Some plants in the treated plot that produced few tomatoes were pulled up during the trial and were not counted
explanation: Not knowing how the fertilizer works does not show that it does not work. (1) is a rival cause, (2) a difference present from the start, and (4) a biased count.

steps.stem: Sales of electric fans at the "Breeze" appliance store rose by forty percent last month. The owner estimated that the rise was due to the heat wave that struck the region during that month. Which of the following data would weaken the owner's estimate?
choices: Sales of air conditioners at the store also rose last month
In the month before, the store's sales fell by fifteen percent
During the heat wave the store cut the prices of all its fans by half
In that month a rival store lowered the prices of its fans
explanation: A price cut at the same time is a rival cause of the rise. (1) supports the heat-wave explanation, and (2) and (4) do not bear on it.

steps.stem: A statistics lecturer found that every one of the history students enrolled in her introductory course regularly hands in the homework late. She concluded that students who take a course outside their own department tend not to bother handing in its homework on time. Which of the following data would strengthen the lecturer's conclusion?
choices: The statistics students enrolled in a course in modern history regularly hand in its homework late
The history students hand in their homework late in all their courses, including their history courses
The statistics students in the introductory course also hand in the homework late
The history department's examination period falls in the middle of the statistics course
explanation: The same pattern in the opposite direction supports the claim about courses outside one's department. (4) supplies another cause, and (2) and (3) show lateness that has nothing to do with the department.

steps.stem: A report on injuries at the Tzur climbing wall over the past five years shows that more climbers were injured while climbing with a safety rope than while climbing without one. Following the report, the wall's manager decided to stop requiring climbers to use a rope, claiming that ropes do not reduce the risk. Which of the following data explains why the manager's claim is mistaken?
choices: The number of climbers at the Tzur wall is small compared with the number at other climbing walls in the region
The number of climbs made with a rope at the Tzur wall is many times the number made without one
At the nearby Eitan climbing wall, more climbers were injured without a rope than with one
Climbers who use a rope pay less attention to their footing than climbers who do not
explanation: More injuries with a rope because there are far more climbs with a rope; the rate of injury per climb may be much lower. (4) explains the count without bearing on the rate, and (1) and (3) are beside the point.

steps.stem: In a study of classroom seating, teachers arranged their pupils' desks in two ways: for one week in a circle, each pupil facing the others, and for one week in rows facing the board. The researchers found that with the desks in a circle the pupils took part in discussions more often, and concluded that pupils who can see their classmates' faces feel freer to speak. Which of the following facts does not weaken the researchers' conclusion?
choices: The week of rows came second, at the end of the term, when many of the pupils were tired from examinations
When the desks were in rows, the pupils at the back of the room found it hard to hear the teacher
The chairs used in the circle arrangement were more comfortable than those used in the rows
Some of the teachers who took part in the study were experienced, and for some it was their first year of teaching
explanation: The teachers' experience does not bear on why the pupils spoke more in the circle. (1), (2) and (3) each offer a reason other than seeing classmates' faces.

steps.stem: Yael's olive tree produced a larger harvest this year than Noam's. Yael attributes the difference to the variety of olive she planted. Noam argues that the difference stems from the fact that Yael's tree grows on a sunny slope, whereas his grows in the shade of a building. Which of the following facts would weaken both claims?
choices: Yael's tree and Noam's tree are of the same variety
Yael's slope is sunny, but it is also very windy
Yael watered and fertilized her tree far more often than Noam did
Yael and Noam watered and fertilized their trees equally often
explanation: Watering and fertilizing are a third cause that is neither the variety nor the sun. (1) tells against the variety alone, (2) touches the sun claim alone, and (4) removes a rival cause instead of adding one.

steps.stem: Most of the bridal shops in the town of Kfar Levanon are clustered on Almond Street. Tal, who has just completed her studies in fashion design, was advised not to open her new bridal shop on that street. Which of the following facts could be a consideration against this advice?
choices: The long-established shops on Almond Street sometimes copy designs from newly opened shops
The town council is about to approve a plan granting reduced municipal taxes to fashion businesses on Almond Street
Most of the fabric suppliers in the region are far from Almond Street, and deliveries there are often delayed
Brides looking for a gown on Almond Street usually start at one end of it, and often tire before they reach the other end
explanation: A benefit available only on that street is a reason to open the shop there. (1) and (3) support the advice, and (4) is neutral.
